property_summary: For every input, the reference contract's version() returns the string "1.0.0"; the mutant changes the returned string so there exist inputs where version() returns a different value (e.g., "2.0.0"), breaking the equality.

For every call to version(), the reference contract always returns the string "1.0.0"; the mutant returns a different string for some inputs (it returns "1.0.1"), so there exists an input where the returned version string differs.

For every input, the reference contract C.version() returns the string "1.0.0"; the mutant returns a different string ("1.0.1") for some input, so there exists a call where the returned string differs.

For every (fuzzed) bytes input used as calldata to call c.version via a low-level call, the reference contract always returns the bytes encoding of string "1.0.0" and the mutant returns a different encoded string for at least one calldata input, so the low-level call's returned data must equal abi.encodePacked("1.0.0") for all admissible calldata.

For every call to c.version() that succeeds, the returned string equals "1.0.0"; the mutant returns "1.0.1" for the same call data, so comparing the returned string bytes against the expected bytes detects the mutant.

For every single-byte calldata input (bytes calldata) sent via a low-level call to address(c).call(data), the reference contract always returns the same 9-byte encoded string "1.0.0" (abi-encoded as a string) when the call succeeds; the mutant returns a different encoded string for at least one such calldata input, so the universal rule is that for all 1-byte calldata values the returned raw returndata equals abi.encodePacked("1.0.0").
For every call, the reference contract's version() returns a non-empty string, whereas the mutant returns an empty string for some input (the function call), breaking the non-empty-return invariant.

For every call, the reference contract's version() returns the string "1.0.0"; the mutant returns a different string ("v1.0.0") for some inputs, so there exists a call where the returned bytes differ.
For any call to version(), the reference contract always returns the exact string "1.0.0"; the mutant returns a different string (e.g. "1.0.0+commit") for some inputs and thus violates this equality.

For every call to version() the reference contract returns the semantic semantic version string "1.0.0"; the mutant returns a different string (e.g. "100") for some inputs, so the returned bytes/string value differs and the equality check fails.
Only the depositorAccount address can successfully call setL1BlockValues (calls from any other address revert).
setL1BlockValues succeeds (does not revert) iff msg.sender equals the contract's depositorAccount (i.e., only depositorAccount can call it)

Only the depositorAccount address can successfully change the L1 block values (i.e., after calling setL1BlockValues, at least one of the public L1 block fields equals the corresponding input only if the caller is depositorAccount).

For all callers, the deployed (reference) contract only allows setL1BlockValues to succeed when msg.sender equals the runtime-stored depositorAccount; the mutant erroneously allows the hard-coded DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT to call successfully, so there exist callers (fuzzed) for which reference rejects but mutant accepts.
